body:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 4, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Approval needed: Auto-rollback on SLO breach — scope + fail-open/fail-closed risk decision

Sean/Rafael,

I’m signing off on the reliability initiative this week and need a crisp recommendation + risk acceptance statement we can reference later.

Two decisions to approve:

1) Scope
- In-scope: latency SLO + error-rate SLO only, used to trigger automatic rollback during model/version rollouts.
- Out-of-scope (explicit): quality/output regressions (handled via separate eval gates), and any “auto-remediation beyond rollback.”

2) Monitoring dependency behavior (fail-open vs fail-closed)
When monitoring is degraded/unavailable/stale (or labels are missing), what’s the safe default?

Options as I understand them:
A) Fail-open: don’t rollback when you can’t confirm a breach (risk: bad rollout keeps hurting users longer).
B) Fail-closed: rollback (or freeze) when you can’t evaluate health (risk: false rollbacks / cascading rollbacks during monitoring outage).

Please reply with:
- your recommended default behavior (and why)
- what we do on UNKNOWN verdict (pause rollout? page? ticket?)
- any guardrails required for leadership comfort (rate limits, min traffic, cooldown, baseline compare)

Goal is to reduce MTTR without creating a new class of incident.

Thanks,
Ava

—
Ava Chen
VP Engineering, Redwood Inference


From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 4, 2025 at 10:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approval needed: Auto-rollback on SLO breach — scope + fail-open/fail-closed risk decision

Agree on scope.

On the monitoring dependency:
- Rolling back on UNKNOWN (monitor outage/staleness) is too risky. We have enough history here: when telemetry/queries go sideways, it’s often broad and correlated. Treating UNKNOWN as BREACH will cause multi-tenant rollback storms.
- Conversely, “do nothing” on UNKNOWN also isn’t acceptable during a rollout, because we’d keep shifting traffic blind.

Recommendation (SRE):
- Auto-rollback should be “fail-open” with respect to the rollback action: i.e., do NOT rollback unless we have a positive breach verdict.
- But rollout progression should be “fail-closed” on UNKNOWN: freeze further traffic increases and require human ack to proceed.

Operationally:
- UNKNOWN verdict triggers a page (not just a ticket) if a rollout is actively changing traffic. If rollout is steady-state (no active increase), ticket is fine.
- Always write audit event: verdict=UNKNOWN, reason=monitor_unavailable/stale/label_mismatch.

Guardrails we consider non-negotiable:
- Minimum traffic before decisioning (to avoid flapping on low-volume routes)
- Warm-up grace period after a rollout step (avoid cold start/initial cache fill triggering rollback)
- Cooldown after rollback action (hard block repeated rollbacks)
- Must-be-worse-than-baseline check where possible
- Per-tenant and global rate limiting on automated rollback actions

Rafael can add paging specifics.

Sean

—
Sean Gallagher
Director, Site Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference


From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 4, 2025 at 11:18 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approval needed: Auto-rollback on SLO breach — scope + fail-open/fail-closed risk decision

+1 to Sean’s framing (rollback requires BREACH, not UNKNOWN).

Paging detail (proposal):
- Page on UNKNOWN only when:
  a) the rollout is in an “active step” (traffic split changing or within warm-up window), AND
  b) the affected scope is non-trivial (e.g., tier=dedicated OR a route with >N req/min in last 30m).
- Otherwise create a ticket and annotate the rollout view as “health signal unavailable.”

What we do for UNKNOWN:
- Freeze traffic shift (keep current split). Do not revert unless we can demonstrate breach.
- Expose “Reason: monitoring unavailable/stale” plus last successful evaluation timestamp.

This also gives oncall a deterministic runbook:
1) Check monitor freshness + labels
2) Check dashboards for broad telemetry issue
3) If underlying service is unhealthy independent of monitoring, manually rollback (explicit human action; audit trail)

This should keep us from repeating the Feb incident class where we took action based on partial/noisy signals.

Rafael

—
Rafael Mendes
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference


From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 4, 2025 at 1:47 PM PT
Subject: Re: Approval needed: Auto-rollback on SLO breach — scope + fail-open/fail-closed risk decision

Thanks — this is the recommendation I was hoping for.

Let me restate the decision in leadership-friendly language (confirm I’m capturing it correctly):

Approved behavior:
- Auto-rollback will trigger ONLY on verified SLO breach (latency/error). If health cannot be evaluated due to monitor/telemetry issues, the verdict is UNKNOWN and we do not automatically rollback.
- However, if the rollout is actively shifting traffic, UNKNOWN will freeze further progression (no additional traffic increase) until human ack.

Oncall signal:
- UNKNOWN during active rollout → page (with scope gating to avoid paging for low-risk/low-traffic).
- UNKNOWN during steady-state → ticket + annotate in console.

I’m comfortable accepting the residual risk that a bad rollout may remain at current canary split longer in an outage scenario, because the alternative (rollback storms) is worse.

Two follow-ups for you both:
1) Please ensure the ADR includes the exact semantics (rollback requires BREACH; UNKNOWN freezes progression; page gating).
2) Please ensure there is a global rollback rate limit / circuit breaker (explicitly documented). I don’t want a single bug to trigger cross-tenant cascade.

If you confirm, I’ll mark this as approved and ask the team to proceed.

Ava


From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 4, 2025 at 2:26 PM PT
Subject: Re: Approval needed: Auto-rollback on SLO breach — scope + fail-open/fail-closed risk decision

Confirming from the Console side: we can represent this cleanly.

We’ll make sure the rollout health view distinguishes:
- HEALTHY
- BREACHING (with which SLO, window, threshold)
- UNKNOWN (monitor unavailable / stale / insufficient traffic)

And the UX will show:
- “Progression paused due to UNKNOWN health” (if in active rollout)
- links to runbook + dashboards
- audit history with the trigger reason + who acknowledged/unpaused

We’ll coordinate exact strings with SRE so oncall doesn’t get surprised by terminology.

Dylan


From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Mar 5, 2025 at 4:48 PM PT
Subject: Re: Approval needed: Auto-rollback on SLO breach — scope + fail-open/fail-closed risk decision

Confirmed.

We’ll update ADR language to be unambiguous:
- UNKNOWN is neither success nor breach; it blocks progressive rollout steps (traffic increases) but does not auto-revert.
- Rollback action requires BREACH verdict AND meeting guardrails (min traffic, warm-up grace, cooldown, baseline compare where available).
- Add circuit breaker:
  - per-tenant rollback max rate (e.g., 1 rollback / X minutes)
  - global cap per region per time window
  - if cap is hit: page + degrade to manual-only

Rafael will bake the paging gating + runbook into oncall docs.

Sean
